Samir to provide private deployment architecture diagram and estimated SLA numbers
Laura to confirm procurement approval timeline (target by 2026-12-08)
Marcus to review KMS/HSM integration notes and share feedback
action_items: Alex Morgan - Send redline copy of MSA + DPA - 2026-12-01

summary: Procurement and legal review of Redwood offering. Main asks: acceptable MSA/DPA terms, SLA targets for Dedicated vs Hosted, pricing approval path, and onboarding timeline. Redwood AE/SE agreed to send redlines, architecture and benchmark docs. Security and legal will follow up on KMS and audit log requirements.
questions: Can Redwood meet a 99.9% uptime SLA for production Dedicated?
Is data at rest always encrypted with customer KMS?
What is the typical onboarding timeline for a VPC/private deployment?
How are audit logs retained and delivered for compliance reviews?
transcript:
Header: 2026-11-28 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Laura Chen (Ember Procurement), Daniel Rivera (Ember Legal), Priya Nair (CTO), Marcus Holt (Security)

00:00 - Alex Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. quick roll call?
00:06 - Laura Chen: yeah this is Laura, procurement, hi.
00:08 - Daniel Rivera: Daniel here from legal.
00:10 - Priya Nair: Priya, CTO, hi.
00:13 - Marcus Holt: Marcus, security engineer.
00:15 - Samir Patel: Samir with Redwood, thanks for having us.
00:18 - Alex Morgan: awesome. agenda - go through MSA/DPA questions, SLAs and pricing approval timeline, then next steps. sound good?

02:02 - Daniel Rivera: yes, and to start, there are a couple of clauses in your standard MSA we usually redline around indemnity and data breach notification windows. typical ask is 48 hours, is that ... is that realistic for you?
02:18 - Alex Morgan: yeah so we can do 48 hours for initial notice, to confirm - we may need some ops time to collect logs, but initial notification 48 hours is acceptable, we can put that in a redline.
02:28 - Daniel Rivera: okay. also about liability caps, Ember prefers per-incident caps above $5M for PHI exposure - that's going to need legal review, but is that something you see in other health customers?
02:43 - Samir Patel: most of our enterprise healthcare customers have negotiated higher caps when they go dedicated, with additional controls like private deployment and encryption keys. we can propose tiered caps tied to Dedicated commitments.
02:58 - Priya Nair: to be clear, we need the private deployment option because of our data residency and on-prem workflow. can you confirm private brings the control plane into our VPC? or is it hybrid? i've seen both.
03:15 - Samir Patel: yep, good question. our Private offering can be deployed with a customer-managed control plane in your VPC, or as an on-prem bundle for air-gapped. for Ember's case we can do VPC with customer KMS. note: sometimes the docs call it "Private" vs "Dedicated" - sorry if that's confusing in the text.
03:33 - Marcus Holt: the KMS bit is critical - do you support HSM-backed keys? and does Redwood ever see the plaintext keys?
03:40 - Alex Morgan: we do support KMS integrations, customers can bring their own keys via supported cloud KMS or an HSM. Redwood never stores raw keys; we use key references and the customer KMS handles unwrapping. we'll add integration notes.

05:12 - Laura Chen: on the DPA, retention terms - Ember needs guaranteed deletion of user PII on request and a retention log for at least 3 years for audits. can you confirm deletion workflows?
05:28 - Samir Patel: yes, we have a documented deletion workflow; on hosted we purge cached prefixes and provide a deletion report. on private, the host controls storage lifecycle so it's directly actionable. we'll include the deletion workflow doc and an example audit report.

07:00 - Daniel Rivera: SLA - we need a 99.9% uptime for production LLM inference. is that for Dedicated only or hosted also?
07:08 - Alex Morgan: right now our SLA table: hosted has a best-effort SLA with credits for platform events; Dedicated includes a 99.9% uptime SLA with defined uptime metrics and support response times. but we can map exact latency SLOs per model in the appendix.
07:25 - Priya Nair: latency SLO is also important - for our clinical triage flow we need p95 generation under 600ms for chat completions at 512 token context. do you have perf numbers?
07:37 - Samir Patel: we do internal benchmarks - for the 13B-class models on a Dedicated pool with tuned quantization we hit p95 around 420-520ms for 512 tokens in our tests, depends on batching and KV cache hit rate. i'll attach the perf sheet.
07:55 - Priya Nair: okay that's promising; would you run a benchmark against our sample dataset?
08:02 - Samir Patel: absolutely, we can run a tailored benchmark as part of the pilot - we'll need a sample prompt set and target QPS.

09:22 - Marcus Holt: audit logs - can you stream audit logs to our SIEM or provide S3 dumps? retention needs to be tamper-evident for compliance.
09:34 - Alex Morgan: yes, audit logs can be exported to customer S3 or streamed to a syslog endpoint. for private deployments it's straightforward; for hosted we offer secure delivery to a customer-owned bucket with immutable retention policies.

11:00 - Laura Chen: pricing approvals - procurement asks timeline: we usually need a PO and final pricing sign-off. what are the typical discounts for an annual Dedicated commit?
11:12 - Alex Morgan: typical committed-cap pricing depends on GPU class and QPS. ballpark, for a 12-month Dedicated commit we can offer 20-30% off list versus on-demand hosted for GPU costs; we'll send a pricing worksheet with line items.
11:27 - Laura Chen: and are there one-time onboarding fees?
11:30 - Alex Morgan: there may be a setup fee for private deployments and engineering onboarding, usually one-time and adjustable based on scope. we'll include that in the quote.

13:05 - Daniel Rivera: procurement wants to understand termination rights and data return timelines post-termination. what does Redwood do for data export?
13:16 - Samir Patel: we provide data export options - snapshots to customer S3, and a documented handoff. retention windows and final deletion are spelled in the DPA; we'll include explicit export SLA (e.g., 30 days).

15:00 - Priya Nair: a couple fine points - model weights handling: if we host open weights in Shared mode vs Dedicated, do you allow customers to pin exact model versions?
15:12 - Alex Morgan: yes, version pinning is supported. Dedicated customers can pin a model build and we can provide a compatible quantized artifact. if you want on-prem, you can run the same pinned version there.

17:20 - Laura Chen: vendor onboarding items - security questionnaire, SOC 2 report, insurance certs. we need SOC 2 Type II and evidence of pentest in last 12 months. do you have those?
17:33 - Alex Morgan: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II and a recent pentest; i'll attach both. we also have an ISO attestation in process.

19:40 - Marcus Holt: one more: are logs redacted by default to remove PHI? how do you handle prompt data?
19:48 - Samir Patel: by default logs contain request metadata and the prompt; customers can opt into full prompt logging or limit retention. for PHI use, we recommend private deployment + no prompt retention and KV cache settings tuned, plus on-prem if required.

21:10 - Daniel Rivera: on liability clause - we'll send proposed language, but is Redwood open to a carve-out if there's gross negligence?
21:21 - Alex Morgan: yes, common to see carve-outs; we'll review your redline and propose language.

23:00 - Priya Nair: onboarding timeline - if procurement signs by 12/08, when could we expect Dev/QA pilot?
23:09 - Samir Patel: typical timeline: 2 weeks for contract finalization, then 2-4 weeks for provisioning and a pilot. so mid-January is reasonable, but if we accelerate engineering onboarding we might start pilot in early January.
23:26 - Laura Chen: procurement will aim for 12/08 approval, that's our internal window.

25:30 - Alex Morgan: quick notes on docs i'll share: redwood MSA template, DPA, private deployment architecture, KMS integration guide, perf benchmark sheet, SOC2 + pentest. links will be in the follow-up email.

27:00 - Daniel Rivera: regarding data residency - Ember requires EU residency for EU customers. can you specify regional deployments?
27:09 - Samir Patel: yes, we can pin region to eu-west for data residency; for private, the control plane and storage can be provisioned in the region.

29:15 - Marcus Holt: about encryption in transit - do you supply mTLS for internal service-to-service?
29:22 - Samir Patel: yes, internal mTLS and customer TLS for ingress. private deployments have mutual TLS by default for control plane communications.

31:00 - Laura Chen: do you have a standard onboarding checklist for procurement? which docs do you need to approve pricing and issue PO?
31:08 - Alex Morgan: we typically need signed MSA + DPA, SOW for Dedicated sizing, insurance cert, and a PO to start billing. procurement template is fine. we'll attach a checklist.

33:45 - Daniel Rivera: small transcribing note: i saw a mention of KV cache earlier - how does that impact data retention?
33:52 - Samir Patel: KV cache is ephemeral; on hosted we can retain prefixes for caching performance but can configure zero retention for PHI workloads. on private, you're in control. we'll document config flags.

35:10 - Priya Nair: compliance question - do you provide penetration test results in redacted form to customers?
35:18 - Alex Morgan: yes, typically redacted pentest reports are shared under NDA; we'll include our latest redacted report in the pack.

37:40 - Laura Chen: to recap next steps: Alex sends redline MSA/DPA and SOC2/pentest, Samir sends architecture + perf sheet and pilot plan, Marcus to share security questionnaire answers, Laura will confirm procurement timeline. everyone okay?
37:55 - Daniel Rivera: yes that aligns.
38:03 - Alex Morgan: great. i'll send a follow-up with attachments and the action item tracker.
38:10 - Samir Patel: and we'll queue a pilot benchmark once Laura sends sample prompts.
38:18 - Priya Nair: thanks everyone.
38:22 - Laura Chen: thanks, bye.

Notes: occasional minor transcription errors (proper nouns sometimes mis-heard), some timestamps approximate. References to docs: https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf , Drive: Ember onboarding folder (link shared in chat).
